added_lines: calendar for the week ahead sunday 1st all saints we celebrate the great company of all those who have gone before us and now enjoy the beatific vision, sharing in god’s life in the glory of heaven. monday 2nd all souls’ day , when the church honours with great respect the memory of the dead and offers her prayers for them . annual mass for the dead at 7.30pm in st pius x church. tuesday 3rd st malachy (1094-1148). as bishop of armagh he continued the reforming work of his predecessor, ceallach. he introduced the cistercians and the canons regular into ireland. returning to ireland from a visit to rome, he revisited clairvaux, where he caught a fever and died in the arms of his friend st bernard. they are buried together. wednesday 4th st charles borromeo (1538-84). a great reforming archbishop of milan after the council of trent. thursday 5th st martin de porres (1579-1639), a dominican lay brother, who spent his nights in prayer and penance and his days caring for the sick and poor. renowned for his devotion to the blessed sacrament. friday 6th all the saints of ireland. we commemorate all our fellow countrymen and women of every age and condition who have gone before us in faith and now enjoy the vision of god. saturday 7th st willibrord (658-739). born in northumbria, he entered the benedictine order and was sent to study in ireland, before going abroad as a missionary. he worked in parts of what is now holla nd, northwest germany and luxembourg. he is remembered as the first of the renowned anglo-saxon missionaries who went to continental europe. first anniversary mass for hugh o’sullivan at 6.30pm. sunday 8th 11.30am mass will be celebrated in ballinacrae. mass this week in st pius x: monday to friday 10am. saturday 6.30pm; a short reflection on today’s gospel matthew 5: 1-12 on the solemnity of all saints, we hear jesus proclaim the beatitudes, showing us the path to true happiness and holiness. in a world that often values success, wealth and recognition, jesus reminds us that god blesses the humble, the merciful, the peacemakers and those who hunger for justice. today, we celebrate not only the great saints whose names we know, but also the countless ordinary people whose quiet lives of faith, love and service reflect the goodness of god. they remind us that holiness is not reserved for a few; it is a calling for every one of us. the beatitudes invite us to live our faith in everyday life: to forgive, to care for those in need, to bring peace where there is division, and to remain faithful through difficult times. as we celebrate all saints, may their example inspire us to follow christ more closely, trusting that even our smallest acts of love can lead us along the path to holiness. lord jesus, through the prayers of all the saints, help us to live the beatitudes each day and become signs of your love in our families, our parish and our community. amen. prayer for vocations to the priesthood : for the future priests of our diocese, the men who will preach the good news of the beatitudes (today's gospel) - the happiness that comes from persevering in faith, and trusting in the goodness and mercy of almighty god through the ups and downs of life. there will be a meeting for anyone considering a vocation to the diocesan priesthood, in derry, on sunday 8th november, beginning at 4pm. for further details, please contact the diocesan vocations director, fr pat o'hagan, at
